title: Why cramming fails
summary: Spreading study across several sessions beats one long session for long-term memory. A little forgetting between sessions actually helps.

scenes.text: Cramming feels effective. For long-term memory, it mostly isn't.
In the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus memorized nonsense syllables to measure forgetting.
The spacing effect: the same study time, spread over several sessions, leads to better long-term memory.

right.label: Spaced
right.text: One hour on three different days

scenes.text: Some forgetting between sessions helps: the effort of remembering again makes memories stronger.
Study a little. Forget a little. Come back.
